name: Handhold — Surgical Clip for Hand Surgery
description: A surgical clip for finger stabilization and incision retraction that interfaces with the Lead Hand surgical positioning system. Designed to reduce operating time and required personnel during hand surgery — used in a live procedure at Spanish Fork Hospital.
highlights: 30+ prototypes refined through direct feedback from three hand surgeons
Met autoclave sterilization requirements for clinical use
Evaluated single-use vs. reusable variants based on market demand and margins
Finalist among 38 teams at the 2026 BYU Student Innovator of the Year competition

name: Pneumatic Continuum Serial Manipulators
description: Engineered and assembled four pneumatic continuum serial manipulators for in-house dynamic modeling research. Performed tensile testing and stress–strain analysis to select spine materials across 12 continuum joints.
highlights: Tensile testing across 12 continuum joints to optimize spine material selection
Assembled and integrated pneumatic joints for experimental validation

name: BYU Mars Rover
award: 3rd Place — 2024 International University Rover Challenge · 102 Universities
description: Led two teams of six engineers to design and integrate the rover's wheel, serial manipulator, elevator, and antenna subsystems. Developed testing procedures that significantly reduced backlash and improved precision in the manipulator arm.
highlights: 3rd place overall among 102 universities worldwide
Highest score among all teams in two of four competition tasks
Quantified joint uncertainty and drove backlash reduction through structured testing

name: Goal Convergence & Obstacle Avoidance — Kuka LBR Arm
description: Built a complete Python kinematics library for a 7-DOF Kuka LBR arm including DH parameterization, forward/inverse kinematics, Jacobian computation, and a potential field obstacle avoidance algorithm for both static and dynamic obstacles.
highlights: Implemented Denavit–Hartenberg parameterization for 7-DOF arm
Potential field methods applied at joints and along links for obstacle avoidance
Generated linear, circular, and spiral dynamic obstacle trajectories for testing

name: Autonomous Ball Scoring Competition Robot
role: ME EN 330: Design of Mechatronic Systems — BYU
award: Highest Score — 2022 ME EN 330 Design Competition · 20 Teams
description: Designed and built an autonomous mechatronic robot to collect, sort, and score black and white ping-pong balls into dynamically changing targets — achieving 29/30 shots and the highest competition score among 20 teams.
highlights: 29/30 successful shots; highest score among 20 competing teams
Flywheel shooting system with color-based servo-actuated ball selection
PIC24 microcontroller in C: line following, sensor fusion, autonomous navigation
Laser-cut & heat-formed acrylic electronics enclosure

name: Personalized Ski Design Optimization Tool
description: A Python optimization framework that generates custom, lightweight ski geometries from user-specific inputs (height, weight, riding style). Integrated a live Onshape CAD model via API to update geometry and retrieve mass at each iteration.
highlights: ~30% mass reduction vs. commercial skis while maintaining performance constraints
Live Onshape CAD integration via API — geometry updates at each optimizer step
SLSQP constrained optimization over length, waist width, camber, thickness

name: Inflatable Robotic Truss — Automated Roller
award: Presented at NASA Big Idea Challenge Forum, Las Vegas
description: Redesigned the automated roller mechanism for an inflatable robotic truss, achieving dramatic weight and cost reductions while doubling structural strength. Engineered a multi-stage gear train using off-the-shelf components to improve torque and reliability.
highlights: 31% weight reduction, 51% cost savings, 2× structural strength
Constructed 21 roller units with custom vise fixtures for precision machining
Presented to NASA planetary scientists at 2024 Big Idea Challenge Forum & LSIC
